display.title: The Best Deal: Reb Meir Refoels and the Tzitzis String
display.summary_short: Reb Meir Refoels gives a roadside peddler all his money for one tzitzis string, and the Alter Rebbe reveals who the peddler really was.
display.summary_long: After the song, the storyteller teaches that everything we do, even eating and earning money, should be for the sake of Heaven, and that a mitzvah is worth more than money, as when Rabban Gamliel paid a fortune for an esrog. He explains when tzitzis with a torn string is still kosher, and why a Chassid fixes it right away anyway. Then comes a story about Reb Meir Refoels after he became a Chassid of the Alter Rebbe. Traveling on business, he notices that his tzitzis are no longer kosher and has his wagon driver stop, refusing to go another step. They wait for hours until a peddler appears at sunset. The peddler at first refuses to unpack for a few strings, then demands all the money Reb Meir has, and Reb Meir gladly hands it over. When the driver calls it highway robbery, Reb Meir answers that this is the best deal he could make. Later, the Alter Rebbe hands Reb Meir back his money and tells him the peddler was Eliyahu HaNavi, sent to test how far he would go for a mitzvah.
display.lesson: A mitzvah is worth any price, and what we give for Hashem comes back to us many times over.

sources_cited.note: Rabban Gamliel paid a great sum for an esrog (as told).
